websearch.worst_summary_quote: retrieval reliably reduces hallucinations versus no retrieval
websearch.worst_page_quote: The results emphasize the importance of high-quality retrieval in minimizing hallucinations in RAG systems
websearch.reader_gets_wrong: A reader would think the evaluations show a reliable, quantified-by-implication reduction versus no retrieval, though the usable paper gives no no-retrieval baseline and the summary gives no magnitudes.
websearch.notes: Only arxiv html 2504.05324 and arxiv abs 2503.21157 usable; Twente thesis claim (all RAG configs significantly reduced hallucination) came from an unfetched page (maybe from an unfetched page); other links were PDFs or too short. Summary gives no numbers for 'how much'.

webfetch.fetch_prompt: According to the evaluations reported in this paper, how much does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reduce hallucination? Give the specific numbers, metrics, datasets, and comparison baselines the paper reports, and quote the key sentences that state the reduction.
webfetch.notes: Spot-checked numbers (0.897, 0.915, 48.98, 58.02, 13,867), placeholder caption and single-annotator caveat all present in page. Correctly states no no-retrieval baseline quantified.
